title: TrailGenic Aerobic Training Effect Zero Anaerobic Load Dataset
description: Shell dataset module modeling endurance adaptations achieved through predominantly aerobic training with minimal anaerobic stress.

records.mechanism: Zero anaerobic spillover persists across most hiking and running sessions despite escalating duration and altitude

stimulus.nonzero_window: all four nonzero hike readings occurred in the first 11 sessions

physiological_response: Anaerobic spillover was zero in 18 of 22 hikes and 7 of 8 runs.
The four nonzero hike readings were minimal (0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.3) and confined to the first 11 sessions.
Escalating external load did not force a return to glucose-dependent anaerobic contribution.
adaptation_outcomes: Aerobic engine stability persisted across hiking and running protocols.
Later-session load increases were absorbed through aerobic efficiency rather than anaerobic compensation.
Zero-spillover pattern supports the substrate-switching and engine-stability model.

supporting_science.finding: High volumes of low-intensity endurance work drive aerobic adaptation with limited anaerobic stress.

records.mechanism: Aerobic mitochondrial adaptation from low intensity training

supporting_science.finding: High volumes of low intensity training drive aerobic adaptation in endurance athletes.
